ambiguities.clauseRef: 90% of net after expenses. Expenses capped $900.
ambiguities.description: The phrase 'after expenses' combined with a cap is ambiguous: does the artist get 90% of (gross minus actual expenses, capped at $900), meaning if actual expenses are $700 the deduction is $700 — or does the cap act as a flat deduction so the artist always nets 90% of (gross minus $900)?

plausibleReadings.summary: Deduct actual expenses up to the $900 cap; if actuals are lower than $900, only actual expenses are deducted.
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable when actual expenses are below $900. On a $5,000 gross with $700 actuals, artist earns 90% of $4,300 = $3,870 vs. $3,690 under p2 — a $180 difference.

plausibleReadings.summary: The $900 cap is treated as a flat deduction regardless of actual expenses, simplifying settlement.
plausibleReadings.impact: Venue-favorable when actuals are below $900. Same example: artist earns 90% of $4,100 = $3,690.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: To confirm before show day: does the $900 expense cap represent the maximum we can deduct (so we only deduct actual expenses up to $900), or is $900 deducted as a flat amount at settlement regardless of what expenses actually come in at?

sourceText: 90% of net after expenses. Expenses capped $900. No guarantee.
